events.body:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7), so extra distance feeds the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies. The trace settles one off-route segment, 17:34–17:42, 4.84 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.00 km, +3.84 km [F3]; the whole trip ran 13.1 km against 8.4 km optimal [F1] on a fixed-route metered service [RD-1].

RD-3 does not exempt this segment: nothing in the record shows a rider-requested stop, let alone a place the rider named that the car stopped at; the only message about a road was the driver asking and the rider refusing [F8][F9][RD-3]. RD-5 does not exempt it either. The only rider words are Chat #2 at 17:31, "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F9] — a refusal, not consent, and it precedes the segment start at 17:34:40. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so there is no unanswered or untimed gap to interpret [F10]. The driver's statement that he asked and took the road anyway [F11] is a post-trip claim, and a driver's assertion of agreement is not consent in any event [RD-5][G11]. RD-4 gives no cover: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F14], and the speed-band records for Ayer Rajah Expressway and Jurong Town Hall Road are band 4 (30–39 km/h) [F12][F13] — neither band 1 nor 2, and in any case speed band alone does not exempt [RD-4].

Amount: the segment's extra 3.84 km × the trip's per-km rate, distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.41 ÷ 13.06 km = $1.4096/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. 3.84 km × $1.4096/km = $5.4129 → $5.41 [F3][F7][RD-2]. I do not refund the remaining gap to the billed excess of $6.53 (4.63 km) [F4], because that difference (map-matching jitter and the 200 m corridor) is not attributable to this segment [RD-2]. The "waiting" charge of $0.11 is meter waiting time under RD-3(c), not an on-trip stop charge, and is not a disputed item here [F5][RD-3]. No prior upheld route dispute in 90 days (route 0 of 1 dispute) [F17], so RD-6 is not triggered and no account flag is raised.

Safety screen: I read Chat #1 and Chat #2 [F8][F9], the driver's statement [F11] and the complaint — there is a route disagreement only, no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; nothing abusive aimed at the other party [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS segment, the meter fare breakdown and a complete timestamped chat record settle every element [F3][F7][F10][G12].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 17:34:40 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 17:31 driver: “Traffic ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Clementi Road?”; F9: Chat #2 17:31 rider: “No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider about the alternative road. The traffic was bad so I took it anyway; it was faster.” (F8, F9, F11)
